t: In front of you is a pair of terraced houses, numbers 213 and 215 King's Road in Chelsea, built in 1720 and now listed Grade II star by English Heritage. The architect Oliver Hill is named as their designer. Hill was a British architect and garden designer who began as a follower of Edwin Lutyens and made his name in the 1920s with country houses. In the 1930s he turned towards modernism, using curving lines and luxurious interiors. He also designed the Midland Hotel in Morecambe and the British pavilion at the 1937 Paris Exposition.
